　一人きりの暗闇は、眩暈がする。
　眩く、心を病みつかせるような、月。

lines.maoEnglish:

An image of cold coursed through my blood.
Alone in the darkness, I grew dizzy.
The moon blazed, dazzling enough to make the heart sick.

“Ah――――”

lines.japanese:
「おはよう翡翠。
今朝も起こしにてきてくれてありがとう」
　ベッドから上半身を起こしながら、できるだけ自然に笑顔を向けた。
「いえ、これがわたしの仕事ですから。
志貴さまに感謝されるほどのことではありません」
「そうかな、俺はすごくありがたいけど。
目覚し時計の音なんかより、何倍もあったかい感じがする」
　ベッドから立ちあがる。
　時刻は朝の七時前―――いつもより十分ほど早い時間。
lines.label: s107
lines.maoEnglish:
“Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for waking me again.”
As I sat up in bed, I gave her the most natural smile I could manage.
“It is only my duty. There is no need for Master Shiki to thank me.”
“Maybe, but I’m really grateful. Waking to your voice feels so much warmer than an alarm clock.”
I rose from bed.
It was not yet seven―――about ten minutes earlier than usual.

“Hey, Ciel. I can’t read these characters.”
―――Rejected.
Or so I’d like to say, but so many people have asked that I’ll answer.
Kura comes from kuramu, ‘to black out’; yami from yamu, ‘to fall ill’; and tsuki means ‘moon’
Put the three together and you get Kurayamizuki.
It is a play on kurayami, ‘darkness.’ Add tsuki, ‘moon,’ and the result is a ‘darkness moon.’
